pr_comments:
Originally, the terminal only received key events if it had focus, meaning if you did something like:
1. focus terminal and hold cmd
2. focus editor and release cmd
and went back to the terminal, it would still behave as though cmd were held down (meaning hovering any path will link to it, even without actually holding down cmd). Similarly, if you hold down the cmd key while in the editor and click into the terminal, the modifier will not register either. Perhaps this could be fixed by having the terminal access global modifier keys instead of maintaining its own modifier state, but I wasn't sure how to go about doing that.

So `global_key_change` just adds a key listener at the global level and no longer requires the element to be in focus for it to trigger.

Rather than patch over the bug with global_key_change, I think it would be better to fix the bug you describe here directly. Any `WindowContext` should have a `modifiers()` method you can use to grab the current global modifier state. Maybe from there, we can pass the modifiers down into `Terminal`, and remove the state entirely?

I just realized WindowContext already has an `on_modifiers_changed` function, which should probably always register global listeners, so I'm considering just taking my logic from `global_key_change` and putting it into `on_modifiers_changed`; does that sound reasonable?
Oh I just checked the code and I've been totally wrong for a while here. There is no global modifiers changed actions! Sorry for the incorrect feedback.
So is this PR fine, or is there still something I should change (aside from resolving merge conflict)?

Hm, it looks like it's still not totally reponsive; sometimes the modifier state doesn't update properly, especially when you rapidly press and release the cmd key.

EDIT: Ah, I see; it was perfectly responsive before https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/15641/commits/e03e45f809e82c0294f5e160d8c1cab256ef15fb, but after adding logic to clear the list of listeners, I think it becomes less responsive since when the terminal is not in focus, the listeners will not be re-registered. I don't know enough about how GPUI works to come up with an elegant solution, so any ideas would be appreciated :)

I'm sorry I've not followed up on this. That said, based on your last comment it looks like the current PR isn't in a good state, and hasn't been touched in a while. I'm going to close this for now, but feel free to open this again if you're still interested :)

issue_context.title: Focus follows mouse
issue_context.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [X] Completed

### Describe the feature

Add a configuration option to send focus to the editor pane (or terminal) under the mouse cursor. AKA `focus follows mouse`.

To elaborate, #4336 describes part of the problem: when you return focus to Zed after activity in another app, the click serves _only_ to focus Zed and does not activate the pane that was actually clicked; rather, the _last active_ pane gets focus. I cannot describe how frustratingly often this bites me - _especially_ when using an integrated terminal in Zed. Having come from desktop Linux many years ago and finding focus-follows-mouse in iTerm2, Zed focuses _exactly the wrong thing_ every single time.

Having:
1. the initial app-focusing click also focus the pane clicked; and
2. focus follow the mouse to whichever editor pane it's over

would be a massive quality of life improvement.

### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help present your vision of the feature


_No response_

Hey @simoncocking, can you check this issue out and see if it covers what you are asking? They feel the same, but not entirely sure - I'll let you make the call:

- https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/4336

Hi @JosephTLyons, I referenced that issue in my description above and commented on it directly a few days ago.

Basically I'd consider what #4336 describes as a _bug_: I expect focus to be directed wherever I _click_, not wherever it was the last time the app had focus. What I'm describing here would be more of a _feature request_: send focus to whichever editor pane is under the mouse cursor.

Focus-follows-mouse has long been a quality-of-life improvement in X Windows desktops. iTerm2/3 supports it on the Mac and it's _wonderful_; it would be equally wonderful in Zed.
